one_liner: Rust benchmarking stub that returns one fixed HTTP response; its README table puts it ahead of nginx 'return 200'.
what_it_does: statico is a command-line HTTP/1.1 server (HTTP/2 and TLS on the tokio runtime only) that answers every request, whatever the path or method, with one configured status, header set and body (inline or @file). Options cover thread count, ports, an artificial delay before the response or the body, a live req/s and Gbps meter, verbose dumps, and a minimal MCP 'everything' mock. It replaces an nginx 'return 200' stub or a hand-written mock upstream in load tests. It is not a general web server: there is no routing, no file tree and no logging.
how_it_is_fast: Thread-per-core design: each worker runs its own single-threaded runtime (current-thread Tokio, or the io_uring runtimes tokio-uring, monoio, glommio, compio) with its own SO_REUSEPORT listener, so the kernel spreads connections and no work moves between threads. The io_uring runtimes bypass hyper: they set up the ring with SINGLE_ISSUER and COOP_TASKRUN (or SQPOLL on request), parse requests with httparse (via the author's http_wire crate) out of one reusable buffer, handle several pipelined requests per read, and write a response serialized once per connection. The default tokio runtime is stock hyper http1 with the body held as a shared Bytes value; mimalloc is the default global allocator.
when_to_use: Upstream for load-testing an HTTP client, load generator, proxy or service mesh, where the backend must never be the bottleneck.
Mock endpoint with a fixed status, headers and body, plus injected latency (--delay, or --body-delay for slow bodies) to test client timeouts.
Measuring the keep-alive HTTP/1.1 request-rate ceiling of a Linux box or NIC with an io_uring runtime and the built-in --meter.
Health-check or MCP mock stub in a CI or test environment.
when_not_to_use: Any real serving: every request gets the same response, with no routing, directory serving, access log or config file.
Facing untrusted clients on the io_uring runtimes: a malformed request is treated as incomplete, so the connection is never answered or closed and its buffer keeps growing.
As evidence that Rust beats nginx: the nginx row was never re-measured alongside the current statico rows, and the nginx configuration, load generator and CPU are unpublished.
HTTP/2, TLS, verbose or body-delay on the io_uring runtimes, which support only HTTP/1.1 (TLS is tokio-only).
Multi-thread scaling on macOS or Windows: SO_REUSEPORT load balancing is enabled only on Linux, FreeBSD, DragonFly, Solaris and illumos.

integration.dependencies: binary crate (cargo install statico): hyper 1, tokio, hyper-util, httparse, http_wire, socket2, rustls/tokio-rustls, clap, pingora-timeout, core_affinity, mimalloc (default feature); optional tokio-uring, monoio + io-uring, glommio, smol + smol-hyper, compio
integration.min_toolchain: Rust edition 2021; no rust-version declared (the io_uring paths use inline const array initialisers, so Rust 1.79 or newer)
integration.platforms: tokio and smol runtimes on Linux, macOS and Windows; tokio-uring, monoio and glommio Linux-only; compio cross-platform (io_uring or IOCP)
integration.thread_safety: Standalone server process; shared config is immutable and counters are sharded atomics, so there is no library API to share
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — it can replace an nginx 'location / { return 200; }' stub in a benchmark or mock setup, but it is not a substitute for nginx as a web server

gotchas: Cross-run baseline: the nginx, HAProxy, Go, Axum and actix-web rows (nginx 286,960 / 379,974 / 832,082) are unchanged since the table first appeared on 2025-12-31 (commit 5e044f0), while the statico rows were re-measured by 2026-03-28. In that original same-run table standard statico was 279,842 vs nginx 286,960 req/s at 1 thread (nginx 2.5% faster) and 966,248 vs 832,082 at 4 threads (1.16x). The README's 'about 40% faster single-threaded' and the doubled io_uring rows (270,263 rising to 589,086 to 656,517) are compared against nginx numbers from the older run.

The io_uring responses are pre-encoded by http_wire, which writes only the status line, the user's headers and Content-Length, so there is no Date header (RFC 9110 requires one from an origin server with a clock) and no Server header, while nginx formats Date, Server and Content-Type per response. Pipelined requests are parsed from one read, but each response is still a separate awaited write_all, not one syscall per batch as the README says.

Unsafe code in the monoio, tokio-uring and compio paths: Vec::from_raw_parts on a pointer into the middle of another Vec's spare capacity, then mem::forget, which breaks Vec's allocation contract. Every http_wire decode error (including malformed requests or more than 128 headers) is treated as 'incomplete', so the connection hangs and grows its buffer 4 KiB per read. The compio runtime's commit is titled 'vibe coded'.

Build drift: the benchmarked build (table last updated 2026-04-25) had neither the current release profile (opt-level 3, fat LTO, 2026-09-12) nor the pinning of every worker to a core (pin_worker, added 2026-09-16). .cargo/config.yaml (target-cpu=native plus LLVM inlining flags) is inert: Cargo reads only config.toml, and the file is cut off mid-array.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick statico when you need a configurable mock or load-test target binary (status, headers, body, delays, metering) rather than a measured server. The HttpArena entries (tokio-uring, the raw tokio server) and routez rest on independent or better-documented harnesses against a pinned nginx build, so cite those for 'beats nginx' evidence.
verified_claims_summary: Author's README table, 1024 connections at 1, 2 and 4 server threads, with no published load generator, CPU, nginx build or nginx config: standard statico (hyper on per-thread Tokio) 399,025 / 1,071,433 req/s vs nginx 'return' 286,960 / 832,082 at 1 / 4 threads, monoio 656,517 / 1,436,420. The nginx row comes from the 2025-12-31 run and was not re-measured with the updated statico rows; in that original run statico was level with nginx on one thread (279,842 vs 286,960) and 1.16x faster on four.
status_note: Active single-maintainer project (v0.18.0, last commit 2026-09-16, 1 star, 0 forks, MIT OR Apache-2.0) and a usable, copyable benchmarking and mocking stub, but its nginx speedup is a cross-run comparison against baseline rows carried over from December 2025 and should not be relied on.
